title: arXiv Trending Biology and Biomedicine — Daily — 2026-11-10
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; attention evidence is sparse, so this is an inferred ranking by relevance and reported evaluation—not a popularity ranking—and arXiv's biomedical coverage is incomplete.

sections.title: Headline
sections.summary: Daily bio/biomed report for the latest announcement batch labeled Tuesday, 10 November 2026. Seven papers are selected from 40 distinct papers across accessible configured category listings. The dominant pattern is computational biology: protein-structure and molecular-dynamics models alongside transcriptomic prediction and evaluation. The snapshot uses the prior batch relative to the UTC calendar date.

sections.title: OriDynamics: Towards a World Model for Biomolecular Dynamics
sections.abstract: OriDynamics generates all-atom conformational ensembles for proteins and protein/ligand complexes, aiming to model both broad state diversity and coordinated atomic fluctuations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved conformational coverage, fluctuation fidelity, and interaction geometry versus leading baselines, with computational examples of alternative states and partner-dependent ensembles.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is structural benchmark and in-silico application work; the preprint does not establish biochemical function or experimentally measured binding/dissociation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct biomolecules-category fit; comparisons across four ensemble benchmark settings. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: Efficient and Accurate Zero Shot Generation of Symmetric Protein Complexes
sections.abstract: ZeUS adapts pretrained SE(3)-equivariant backbone generators to create symmetric protein assemblies without retraining, by generating a canonical subunit and using symmetry-aware computation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report comparable designability and diversity to full-complex inference with predicted O(k) memory and runtime savings, and generation of very large symmetric backbones.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that biological validity at the largest scales remains untested: these are backbone-only structures, and designability is intractable for the largest examples.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct biomolecules-category fit; arXiv notes NeurIPS 2026 publication and the paper compares three backbone models across symmetry settings. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: stMIND: Learning multiscale interaction dynamics from spatial-temporal transcriptomics
sections.abstract: stMIND infers continuous gene-expression, spatial, and proliferation dynamics from unmatched spatial-transcriptomics snapshots by modeling cell-intrinsic, local, and nonlocal influences.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report stronger short-horizon expression prediction and spatial coherence on axolotl regeneration and zebrafish development datasets, and infer a 10–15-day post-injury transition in axolotl telencephalon.
sections.unique_caveat: Dynamics and interaction operators are inferred from destructive, unmatched snapshots rather than tracked cells; at long horizons the paper reports that a non-spatial baseline has lower expression error.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct quantitative-biology listing; evaluation on axolotl and zebrafish data against four baselines, with five random seeds reported. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: HyPLM Technical Report
sections.abstract: HyPLM-Flash is a 650-million-parameter protein language model and inference engine that the authors present as a compute-efficient alternative for protein representation tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report training on 726 billion tokens, throughput around 130,000 residues/s on one NVIDIA H20 GPU, and competitive results across a 32-task benchmark suite.
sections.unique_caveat: These are author-reported computational benchmarks; throughput is hardware- and implementation-dependent, and benchmark performance is not experimental validation of protein function.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in machine learning and biomolecules; the technical report compares 28 public checkpoints across 32 tasks. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: scBIG++: Learning Across Genes and Cells to Predict Single-Cell Perturbation Responses
sections.abstract: scBIG++ predicts full-gene single-cell expression responses to genetic or chemical perturbations while modeling heterogeneity across cells and shared gene modules.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report competitive recovery of perturbation effects and reconstruction across all assayed protein-coding genes retained after preprocessing.
sections.unique_caveat: The contribution is prediction on benchmark data; it does not show that predicted gene-expression changes reproduce in new wet-lab perturbation experiments.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in genomics, machine learning, and AI; evaluation spans six perturbation settings, including unseen targets, combinations, and transfer settings. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: KineCouple: Substrate-conditioned residual readout for enzyme kinetic prediction
sections.abstract: KineCouple uses substrate-conditioned attention over protein residues to predict enzyme kcat and Km values from sequence and substrate representations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report small improvements over reproduced CataPro results for both kcat and Km prediction.
sections.unique_caveat: Reported gains are marginal (kcat RMSE 1.333 to 1.330 and Km RMSE 0.998 to 0.997); these are prediction metrics, not biochemical assay results.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in AI and quantitative biology; v2 is the substantive update in the selected batch, evaluated on pooled out-of-fold CataPro predictions. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: When gene summaries reveal the answers: Gene Ontology circularity in gene embedding benchmarks
sections.abstract: The paper tests whether gene-description text already contains Gene Ontology labels used to evaluate gene embeddings, and proposes a benchmark for comparing models with matched input text.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that removing generated GO-derived summaries reduces function-prediction AUROC in several settings and introduce GeneProv to evaluate text/label provenance and non-GO endpoints.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper says its historical GO scorer mishandled ties and the original predictions were unavailable for rescoring, limiting exact reproduction of some estimates.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in machine learning and genomics; analysis covers 19,256 human protein-coding genes with checks in mouse and yeast. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: Protein modeling appears in ensembles and scalable assembly generation (OriDynamics, ZeUS, HyPLM-Flash). Transcriptome methods infer spatial-temporal gene expression (stMIND) and perturbation responses (scBIG++). Evaluation reliability recurs in enzyme-kinetics metrics (KineCouple) and gene-function benchmark provenance (GeneProv). These are repeated themes in the selected set, not evidence of an arXiv-wide shift.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: OriDynamics and ZeUS motivate independent biochemical or structural validation, especially for large backbone-only designs. stMIND could be checked against lineage-tracked or held-out spatial time-series data and perturbations of predicted local versus nonlocal influences. scBIG++ and KineCouple need external intervention and enzyme-substrate evaluations, ideally with new measured outcomes. GeneProv motivates matched-text splits, independent annotation sources, and benchmark scorer/prediction preservation. These are proposed follow-ups, not clinical advice or claims of novelty.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: This batch is strongest in computational protein modeling and transcriptomic inference, with benchmark reliability as a recurring concern. Independent experimental, temporal, and out-of-distribution checks remain the key uncertainty; these are notable recent papers, not established biological or clinical results.
